assets.content:
Subject: Website chat, one support inbox
Preview text: Test the complete workflow on your store for 14 days, with no card required.

Bring website chat into one support inbox

Hi there,

With the Crisp chat widget installed on your store site, customers can start a conversation there while your team handles it through one omnichannel inbox alongside other support conversations.

Crisp is a customer support platform that combines website chat with an omnichannel support inbox. It gives your team one place to work from instead of treating live chat as a separate inbox.

If the workflow fits, a Crisp Paid plan offers flat pricing for up to 20 users.

Test it on your own site with a 14-day free trial. All Crisp features are included, and no card is required before you decide whether it works for your team.

Start your 14-day free trial → https://app.crisp.chat/initiate/signup/?locale=en

- Crisp

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team wants website chat alongside other support channels, it can handle those customer conversations in one omnichannel inbox rather than treating live chat as a separate inbox.
value_case.mechanism: After the Crisp chat widget is installed on the site, the team can handle its chat conversations through Crisp's omnichannel support inbox. Crisp also offers a flat-price Paid plan for up to 20 users.

The flat-price statement applies to a Crisp Paid plan for up to 20 users; no specific price or comparative savings figure is established.

Do not promise: Any promise of zero disruption when migrating from an incumbent helpdesk

selected_brief.single_idea: Crisp lets an ecommerce support team run website chat and handle customer conversations in one omnichannel inbox, with 14 days to test all Crisp features without a card.
selected_brief.felt_need: Small ecommerce support teams report that per-seat or rising subscription costs on helpdesk/live-chat tools like Zendesk strain their budget, driving active comparison and eventual switching to cheaper alternatives.
selected_brief.mechanism: Once the Crisp chat widget is installed on the store site, its customer conversations can be handled through Crisp's omnichannel support inbox. The reader can try this setup during a 14-day trial that includes all Crisp features and requires no card.
selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: Crisp may seem like another support tool requiring a purchasing decision upfront. After: it is a specific website-chat and omnichannel-inbox setup the team can run on its own site for 14 days with all features and no card.

That every recipient currently uses Intercom, Zendesk, Tidio, Shopify, WooCommerce, Gmail, or any other named tool.
That Crisp is cheaper than a named competitor; the evidence establishes only a flat-price Paid plan for up to 20 users without a dollar amount.
Security, compliance, uptime, migration, AI Agent, Magic Replies, chatbot, or automation claims; they distract from this email's single workflow and next step.
Any guarantee that the product will suit every ecommerce support team or produce Decathlon's, Reedsy's, or another customer's results.
selected_brief.objection: “I do not want to pay or provide a card before I know whether this workflow fits our store.”
selected_brief.tone: Direct, practical, and confident without hype.
selected_brief.next_step_decision: Decide whether Crisp is suitable for running the store's website chat and handling customer conversations through one omnichannel support inbox before choosing a paid plan.
selected_brief.next_step_value: The signup opens a 14-day trial with all Crisp features and no card required, allowing the team to install the widget and try the documented inbox workflow on its own site.
selected_brief.next_step_limit: The trial does not by itself establish migration effort, comparative savings, Shopify or WooCommerce order-history access, or support for spam filtering, bulk actions, email search, and formatting retention.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Earn the open with the concrete operational change—website chat and other support conversations in one inbox—and signal that the reader can test it for 14 days without a card; avoid vague AI language, inflated savings claims, and named-competitor attacks.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Crisp offers a website chat widget connected to one shared support inbox, which could let my team handle chat and other customer conversations in one place.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The offer fits the explicitly selected situation: a cost-sensitive ecommerce support team considering a replacement for Intercom or Zendesk. The store site and support team are established by the profile, but our current tool, whether chat is currently separate, and whether consolidating channels would improve our workflow are unknown. The email presents the trial conditionally rather than claiming those unknowns as facts.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: we operate an ecommerce store with a small customer-support team and are cost-sensitive while considering replacement support software.
Email-only: customers currently need or would use a website chat widget.
Email-only: our team has other support conversations that can be handled alongside website chat in Crisp's omnichannel inbox.
Email-only: treating live chat as a separate inbox is currently a workflow problem for us.
Not established: we currently use Intercom, Zendesk, Tidio, Shopify Inbox, or any particular support tool.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Finding a cost-effective replacement is relevant now because it defines the selected audience. Whether separate chat inboxes are an active problem for my team is unknown, and consolidation could itself introduce workflow friction. The email does not give enough pricing detail to judge the main cost concern.
reader_verdicts.stopped_at: If the workflow fits, a Crisp Paid plan offers flat pricing for up to 20 users.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: For a cost-sensitive replacement decision, “flat pricing” is not enough: I still do not know the paid plan's actual price, so I cannot tell whether testing and installing it is worth the effort.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me the exact paid-plan price for a team of up to 20 users.
fixes: Rewrite “If the workflow fits, a Crisp Paid plan offers flat pricing for up to 20 users.” as “After the trial, the relevant paid plan costs [exact amount and billing period] for up to 20 users.”
Rewrite “alongside other support conversations” to name the specific conversation channels included, so I can tell whether this could replace my current workflow without guessing.
Rewrite “Test it on your own site with a 14-day free trial.” to briefly state what installing the test requires and whether it can be removed without disrupting the existing support setup.

brief.promise: Crisp gives an ecommerce support team website chat and one omnichannel inbox for customer conversations, with a 14-day all-features trial that requires no card before the team decides whether it fits.
brief.orientation: Crisp is a customer support platform that provides a website chat widget and a single omnichannel inbox where a store's team handles customer conversations.
brief.arc: In one email, move the reader from recognizing Crisp as another support-platform option to understanding the specific store workflow it enables and seeing a low-commitment way to test that workflow.
brief.sequence_rationale: One email is sufficient because the request explicitly requires one introduction and one next step. Lead with the operational value—website chat plus an omnichannel inbox—because that gives the reader a concrete reason to want Crisp. Use the flat-price Paid plan for up to 20 users as relevant commercial context without claiming savings, then make the 14-day all-features, no-card trial the single action. This order gives a solution-aware buyer the product, its useful operation, and the evaluation path without turning the email into a feature catalogue or unsupported competitor comparison. No separate objection or migration email is warranted, and the unsupported inbox-friction problem is excluded. Can this source be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

emails.selection_reason: This combines the most relevant documented operation for an ecommerce support team—handling website chat and other inbound conversations in one omnichannel inbox—with commercial terms that make a first evaluation concrete for a cost-sensitive buyer.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team wants website chat alongside other support channels, it can handle those customer conversations in one omnichannel inbox rather than treating live chat as a separate inbox.
value_case.mechanism: After the Crisp chat widget is installed on the site, the team can handle its chat conversations through Crisp's omnichannel support inbox. Crisp also offers a flat-price Paid plan for up to 20 users.
decision_conditions: The Crisp chat widget must be installed on the buyer's site to run the proposed chat workflow.
The flat-price statement applies to a Crisp Paid plan for up to 20 users; no specific price or comparative savings figure is established.

emails.target_audience: Cost-sensitive ecommerce support team replacing Intercom/Zendesk
emails.job: Get the reader to start a 14-day trial and test Crisp's website-chat and omnichannel-inbox workflow on their own site.
emails.single_idea: Crisp lets an ecommerce support team run website chat and handle customer conversations in one omnichannel inbox, with 14 days to test all Crisp features without a card.
emails.felt_need: Small ecommerce support teams report that per-seat or rising subscription costs on helpdesk/live-chat tools like Zendesk strain their budget, driving active comparison and eventual switching to cheaper alternatives.
emails.mechanism: Once the Crisp chat widget is installed on the store site, its customer conversations can be handled through Crisp's omnichannel support inbox. The reader can try this setup during a 14-day trial that includes all Crisp features and requires no card.
emails.belief_shift: Before: Crisp may seem like another support tool requiring a purchasing decision upfront. After: it is a specific website-chat and omnichannel-inbox setup the team can run on its own site for 14 days with all features and no card.
must_not_say: Any claim that Shopify or WooCommerce order history is consolidated into the inbox.
Any savings figure or superiority claim versus Intercom, Zendesk or Tidio.
Any promise of zero disruption when migrating from an incumbent helpdesk.
Any promise of reduced headcount, growth or response-time improvement for this buyer.
Any specific monthly price for the flat-price plan.
Any claim that Crisp resolves spam segregation, bulk conversation actions, email formatting retention, or email search inside the consolidated inbox.
That every recipient currently uses Intercom, Zendesk, Tidio, Shopify, WooCommerce, Gmail, or any other named tool.
That Crisp is cheaper than a named competitor; the evidence establishes only a flat-price Paid plan for up to 20 users without a dollar amount.
Security, compliance, uptime, migration, AI Agent, Magic Replies, chatbot, or automation claims; they distract from this email's single workflow and next step.
Any guarantee that the product will suit every ecommerce support team or produce Decathlon's, Reedsy's, or another customer's results.
emails.objection: “I do not want to pay or provide a card before I know whether this workflow fits our store.”
emails.tone: Direct, practical, and confident without hype.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Crisp is suitable for running the store's website chat and handling customer conversations through one omnichannel support inbox before choosing a paid plan.
emails.next_step_value: The signup opens a 14-day trial with all Crisp features and no card required, allowing the team to install the widget and try the documented inbox workflow on its own site.
emails.next_step_limit: The trial does not by itself establish migration effort, comparative savings, Shopify or WooCommerce order-history access, or support for spam filtering, bulk actions, email search, and formatting retention.
emails.subject_strategy: Earn the open with the concrete operational change—website chat and other support conversations in one inbox—and signal that the reader can test it for 14 days without a card; avoid vague AI language, inflated savings claims, and named-competitor attacks.
